core_claim: The NBA's Last Two Minute Report shows late-game officiating is 91% correct in aggregate — but its remaining errors are concentrated on specific call types (missed travels, missed defensive 3-seconds), specific positions (guards get hurt, bigs get charged), and specific games (Scott Foster shows up in the worst ones) in patterns the popular lore gets wrong.

edt_01.label: Hook — first time the NBA said we were wrong
edt_01.title: The first time the NBA said 'we were wrong'
edt_01.editorial_notes: The 91.23% and 29.58/61.65/0.96/7.81 breakdown must be exact.

edt_02.label: The 8:1 asymmetry
edt_02.title: When the refs get it wrong, they get it wrong by silence
edt_02.editorial_notes: 63.6% missed defensive 3-seconds and 43.9% missed travels are the headline numbers of this section — do not round.

edt_03.label: Errors per game
edt_03.title: One admitted mistake per game
edt_03.editorial_notes: 1.49 mean, 28.9% clean games, 14-error max are the anchors.

edt_04.label: Getting better over time
edt_04.title: The league is getting better — fast
edt_04.editorial_notes: 13.03% -> 6.15% arc is the core. Mention the caveat about scope change in 2017-18 but don't let it overshadow the trend.

edt_05.label: Scott Foster test
edt_05.title: The Scott Foster test
edt_05.editorial_notes: 49 of 59 ranking is the pivot point. Keep 'below median, not an outlier' exactly as worded.

edt_06.label: Referee spread
edt_06.title: The refs are more similar than the lore says
edt_06.editorial_notes: Min-to-max spread is 4.42 points. The 'entire league' spread framing is important.

edt_07.label: Home bias isn't
edt_07.title: The home-court bias that isn't
edt_07.editorial_notes: 49.88 vs 50.12 split. Note that published research on different samples has found small biases — the editor explicitly says our clean window shows 50/50. Do not overclaim.

edt_08.label: Positional asymmetry
edt_08.title: The real asymmetry is positional, not personal
edt_08.editorial_notes: Gortat -38 and Wiggins +15 are the tent-poles. LeBron's near-neutrality (-5 of 477) is the counter-intuitive finding that kills the 'superstar calls' myth.

edt_09.label: Buzzer is not where mistakes happen
edt_09.title: The buzzer isn't where the mistakes happen
edt_09.editorial_notes: 6.62% at 0-9s, 10.07% at 40-49s. Most surprising tick in the dataset.

edt_10.label: Close — transparency paid off
edt_10.title: What transparency actually changed
edt_10.editorial_notes: Close on the tension: union hates it, the numbers endorse it. No summary, end on the PDF-in-the-morning line.
